map.Token 用量估算是做什么的？: What does Token Usage Estimator do?
map.如何使用Token 用量估算？: How do I use Token Usage Estimator?
map.Token 用量估算适合哪些场景？: What scenarios is Token Usage Estimator best for?
map.按中英文与代码估算 token 用量。: Estimate token usage by the mix of Chinese, English and code.
map.tokens ≈ 中文字数 / 1.5 + 英文词数 / 0.75 + 代码字符: tokens ~ Chinese chars / 1.5 + English words / 0.75 + code characters
map.混合内容按三类分别折算：中文按字符、英文按词、代码按字符（切分最碎）。这是粗略预: Mixed content is converted by three classes: Chinese by character, English by word, code by character (split finest). This is a rough budgeting tool; actual values fluctuate +/-20% with tokenizer and symbol density, so leave a safety margin when judging whether you are near the context limit.
map.不同分词器差异较大，仅供参考。: Tokenizers differ greatly; for reference only.
map.按中英文与代码比例估算文本 token 数，提示不同分词器差异。: Estimate text token counts by the ratio of Chinese, English and code, and note the differences across tokenizers.
map.中文约 1~2 字/token(因模型而异)，英文约 4 字符/token，代码: Chinese is about 1-2 chars/token (model-dependent), English about 4 chars/token, and code is denser.
map.估算用于把控上下文窗口与 API 成本，精确值需对应模型分词器计数。: The estimate helps manage the context window and API cost; the exact value needs the corresponding model tokenizer count.
map.一段 500 中文字+200 英文词：中文≈500×1.5=750 token，: A passage of 500 Chinese chars + 200 English words: Chinese ~ 500 x 1.5 = 750 tokens, English ~ 200 x 1.3 = 260 tokens, total ~ 1010 tokens. Actual results deviate by model tokenizer.
map.为什么中文 token 数不固定？: Why is the Chinese token count not fixed?
map.不同模型对中文的子词切分不同(按字/按词/混合)，同一段中文 token 数可差: Different models subword-split Chinese differently (by char / by word / mixed), so the same Chinese passage can differ several times in token count; this estimate only gives magnitude, and exact counts need the corresponding tokenizer.
map.代码为什么更费 token？: Why does code consume more tokens?
map.代码含大量符号、缩进与标识符，信息密度高、子词切分更碎，同等字符数常比自然语言消: Code contains many symbols, indentation and identifiers, with high information density and finer subword splits, so the same character count often consumes more tokens than natural language.
